title: How to Extend the Life of Your Deck with Seasonal Maintenance
seoTitle: Deck Seasonal Maintenance to Extend Its Life
seoDescription: What to inspect, clean, seal and prepare each season to help your wood deck last longer, plus when to send a deck repair request near Collingwood.
html:
The biggest enemy of a wood deck isn’t foot traffic. It’s trapped moisture. When water sits on or in wood, it promotes rot, splits, and the conditions that hardware corrosion needs to take hold. Seasonal maintenance is essentially a systematic effort to keep wood dry and protected. Catching problems early prevents the kind of damage detailed in Signs Your Deck Needs Repair Before It Becomes a Safety Hazard.

Spring: Inspect and Clean

Start each season with a thorough inspection. Then pressure wash the deck surface to remove the previous year’s mould, mildew, and grime. Use a deck wash solution on older wood before power washing to lift embedded organic material.

Check the gaps between deck boards. They should be consistent and open. Boards that have swollen and closed the gaps trap moisture and create rot conditions. A circular saw set to the right depth can re-establish gaps if needed.

Summer: Seal and Protect

Apply a quality deck sealant or stain every year or two for pressure-treated lumber, or annually for older untreated wood. The right product depends on the wood species and the existing finish. A penetrating oil-based sealer works best on weathered wood. A film-forming stain or paint provides more durable surface protection on newer lumber.

Don’t apply sealant in direct sunlight or extreme heat. It flash-dries before penetrating properly. A cool, cloudy day with no rain forecast for 24 to 48 hours is ideal.

Fall: Prep for Winter

Clear all deck furniture and planters before freeze season. Standing planters concentrate moisture and create rot conditions in the boards beneath them. Move furniture at least enough to allow the deck surface to dry fully.

Do a final inspection of all fasteners. Tighten anything that’s loosened over the season, and hammer down any nail heads that have lifted. Check that deck drain paths are clear so snow melt doesn’t pond on the surface. For cottage owners, the same fall preparation logic applies. See the cottage closing checklist for the full winter prep walkthrough.

When to Get Help

Soft or rotted boards, loose railings, wobbly stairs or posts that move are repair jobs, not maintenance. Keep people off unsafe areas. To get help, send a request through Collingwood Handyman with photos of the deck surface, the underside and any damaged areas. A local service provider can review the request and confirm whether the job is within scope. Structural rebuilds or new decks may need a deck builder and a permit, so confirm with the Town of Collingwood or your municipality.
